rendered: The LLTO coating that retained the most capacity after 200[1] cycles at 0.5C[2] was LLTO-2[3], at 86.2%[4]. For comparison, the other LLTO coatings retained 85.5%[5] (LLTO-0.5) and 57.2%[6] (LLTO-1). The document states that the pristine NCM[7] only retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles[8]. So the best LLTO coating (LLTO-2) kept a far larger share of its capacity than the pristine NCM over the same cycling. Rate capability: LLTO coating in general improved it, which the document attributes to the high ionic conductivity of the LLTO layer and to suppression of undesirable side reactions between the electrolyte and the cathode surface. With the 2[9] mol.% coating, however, rate capability decreased. The document attributes this to the coating getting thicker: thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron[10] transfer process during charge/discharge cycling[11]. In other words, the thicker layer impeded electron transfer during charge and discharge. The document gives no rate-capability values for the LLTO coatings, so the size of the drop is not quantified.
